contentBlocks.text: Last week you solved systems of equations. This week: exponent rules, one of this course's other core threads!

When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: x³ · x⁴ = x⁷ (since x³ · x⁴ = (x·x·x)·(x·x·x·x), seven x's total). When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents: x⁷ / x³ = x⁴. Simplify x⁵ · x² and y⁸ / y³ using these rules.
You just learned to multiply and divide powers! Tomorrow we'll learn what happens when you raise a power to another power.

objectives: State the product-of-powers rule: add exponents when multiplying same-base powers
State the quotient-of-powers rule: subtract exponents when dividing same-base powers
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's systems-of-equations work briefly.
2. Introduce the product and quotient rules, expanding x³·x⁴ by hand to show why it works.
3. Have the child simplify x⁵·x² and y⁸/y³.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's power-of-a-power lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: physically expand a small example (x²·x³) into repeated multiplication before introducing the shortcut rule
Ready for more: ask the child what happens when the bases are DIFFERENT (e.g. x³·y⁴) and why the rule doesn't apply there

generationData.instructions: Simplify each expression using the product or quotient rule.
